```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(AKCatchments)
options(AKCatchments.cache = file.path(tempdir(), "ak_vignette_cache"))
```

Shares of each NLCD Level II class in each catchment from the NLCD 2016
Alaska release (Dewitz 2019, doi:10.5066/P96HHBIE; 30 m), the most recent
NLCD land cover for Alaska. Optionally bias-adjusted with an error matrix
(Olofsson et al. 2014).

Input, as for every layer: catchments (sf polygons with `site_code`, one
row per catchment, any CRS; a single `ak_delineate()` result, a list of
them, `ak_catchments()` output or your own polygons). Chunks that download
data are not run when this vignette is built; chunks that only compute
are. The other layers are listed in `vignette("delineation")`, section 7.

## 1. Getting the data

Automatic, once: the statewide raster is downloaded from ScienceBase (the
link is looked up in the item record, since direct file links have changed
before) into the cache's `nlcd_2016_ak/` folder.

```{r prefetch, eval = FALSE}
ak_prefetch(x, layers = "landcover/nlcd2016")
```

## 2. Using it

```{r use, eval = FALSE}
d <- ak_delineate(lat = 63.7255, lon = -148.9670, site_code = "SITE-001")   # one catchment
ak_landcover(d)                                     # one catchment: its row with the columns added

x <- ak_catchments(pts)                                  # many: data frame of site_code, lat, lon
x <- ak_landcover(x)                            # columns appended to x, provenance recorded
ak_provenance(x)

ak_landcover(sf::read_sf("hand_catchments.gpkg"))            # your own polygons with site_code (or import_catchments())
```

With an error matrix of reference-sample counts (rows map class, columns
reference class, both named with NLCD codes such as `"41"`):

```{r adjust, eval = FALSE}
ak_landcover(x, error_matrix = em)          # adds nlcd_adj_pct_<class> with _se, _lo95, _hi95
```

## 3. What you get

`nlcd_pct_<class>` (percent of the mapped part; classes `water`,
`icesnow`, `dev_open` ... `woody_wetland`, `herb_wetland`),
`nlcd_pct_coverage_pct`, `nlcd_flag` (`no_2016_assessment` always,
`small_catchment` under 1 km², `partial_coverage`). With `error_matrix`:
`nlcd_adj_pct_<class>` and its `_se`, `_lo95`, `_hi95`.

## 4. Uncertainty: how it is computed

**Product error (P).** No accuracy assessment exists for the 2016 Alaska
map. The only Alaska assessment is for NLCD 2001: overall accuracy 76.2%
(s.e. 2.8%) at Level II with primary-or-alternate reference labels, and
59.4% with primary labels only (Selkowitz and Stehman 2011). Accuracy was
higher for common classes and patch interiors.

**Calculation.** Without an error matrix, `ak_landcover()` reports the
mapped shares with `nlcd_flag` (`no_2016_assessment` always,
`small_catchment` under 1 km², `partial_coverage`). With an error matrix
of **sample counts** (rows = map class, columns = reference class, NLCD
codes as names), it adds bias-adjusted shares with SE (Olofsson et al.
2014): the adjusted share of class *k* is Σᵢ Wᵢ nᵢₖ / nᵢ., where Wᵢ is the
catchment's mapped share of class *i*, and its variance is Σᵢ Wᵢ² qᵢₖ(1 −
qᵢₖ) / (nᵢ. − 1), with qᵢₖ = nᵢₖ / nᵢ.:

```{r olofsson}
em <- matrix(c(40, 0, 10, 50), 2, dimnames = list(map = c("forest", "shrub"), reference = c("forest", "shrub")))
em                                       # 50 mapped-forest pixels checked: 40 forest, 10 shrub; 50 mapped-shrub: all shrub
adjust_class_shares(c(forest = 70, shrub = 30), em)
```

The map says 70% forest; one in five mapped-forest pixels is really
shrub and no mapped-shrub pixel is forest, so the adjusted share is 0.7 x
0.8 = 56%. Misclassification **biases**
shares, not just blurs them.

**Assumptions.** The regional matrix applies inside each catchment; the
2001 matrix applies to the 2016 map; the reference sample was stratified
by map class. The SE reflects the size of the reference sample, not
catchment-specific error, so it is the same order for every catchment.

**Alternatives.** No adjustment (biased shares, no SE); a matrix from your
own reference points; another product with its own published matrix
(ESA WorldCover). The choice of matrix moves every catchment the same way,
so it shifts means and intercepts more than it changes rankings.

**Downstream.** Shares are compositional: they sum to 100 and their errors
are negatively correlated (pixels moved out of one class go into another).
Don't put all classes in one model, and expect the adjustment to move
correlated classes together.

## 5. Checking and validating it

- **Build your own error matrix** from reference points (field plots, or
  points labelled on high-resolution imagery), stratified by map class:

```{r own-matrix, eval = FALSE}
pts <- sf::read_sf("lc_reference_points.gpkg")              # a `reference` column with NLCD codes
map <- terra::extract(terra::rast(list.files(ak_cache_dir("nlcd_2016_ak"), "\\.(tif|img)$",
                                             recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)[1]),
                      terra::vect(sf::st_transform(pts, 3338)))[[2]]
em <- table(map = map, reference = pts$reference)
ak_landcover(x, error_matrix = unclass(em))
```

- **Another product.** ESA WorldCover 2021 (10 m; live test P05 reads it)
  gives an independent classification; compare shares of forest, shrub,
  water and ice at your sites.
- **Glacier and water shares** can be checked against RGI glaciers
  (`vignette("glaciers-rgi")`) and the imagery plots.

## 6. Pitfalls

- Shares are compositional: errors in one class come out of others.
- The 2016 map has never been assessed; 2001 accuracy applied to 2016 is
  an assumption.
- Small catchments are mostly patch edges, where accuracy is lowest.

## References

- Dewitz, J. (2019). National Land Cover Database (NLCD) 2016 products. USGS data release, doi:10.5066/P96HHBIE.
- Olofsson, P. et al. (2014). Good practices for estimating area and assessing accuracy of land change. Remote Sensing of Environment 148, 42-57.
- Selkowitz, D. J. and Stehman, S. V. (2011). Thematic accuracy of the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) 2001 land cover for Alaska. Remote Sensing of Environment 115, 1401-1407.
